sourcedFrom: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer (2014 — read from the document's own footer)
cleanIntro: The F3 SuperTrap is a break-action over-under with a SELF-COCKING double lock — opening the gun cocks both locks, and one is still cocked after a shot. ⚠ Two things set it apart from an ordinary O/U on the bench. First, Blaser fits a STRIKER SAFETY CATCH system that works independently of the safety slide, and it has a handling consequence: touching the trigger while closing the gun can block the strikers. Second, the SuperTrap has an adjustable RIB — §6 of Blaser's book is this model's own section, and its point of impact is set with a click-indexed rail screw rather than by bending anything.

steps.title: ⛔ The safety catch will not hold a dropped gun
steps.action: Pull the safety catch lever BACK with your thumb until S is visible. ⛔ Then read Blaser's own DANGER block and believe it: heavy jolting or dropping this gun can disengage the locks despite the safety being on. The safe state for a bench session is open and empty, not secured.
steps.prose: A maker's warning about the limits of his own safety catch is the most useful sentence on the page.
steps.aside: Pull safety catch lever back with thumb. S (= Safe) is visible. Gun is secured.
steps.quote: Heavy jolting or dropping the gun can cause locks to disengage, despite the gun being safety-secured.
steps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 5.3. Securing the gun — DANGER

steps.title: ⚠ Do NOT touch the trigger as the gun closes
steps.action: The F3 carries a STRIKER SAFETY CATCH system that is independent of the safety slide position — and Blaser adds the handling rule that goes with it: when closing the gun the trigger should not be touched, because doing so can make one safety sear block the strikers.
steps.prose: A gun that will not fire after a clean is sometimes a gun that was closed with a finger in the wrong place.
steps.quote: The F3 is fitted with a striker safety catch system that is independent of the safety slide position. When closing the gun the trigger should not be touched as this can cause one safety sear to block the strikers.
steps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 5.5. Loading the gun — NOTE

steps.title: Open it — and read what the extractors do
steps.action: Secure the gun, press and hold the locking lever, and tip the barrel set down about 45°. Each barrel has an extractor WITH an ejector function, and the ejector is only live on a barrel that has been FIRED — so fired cases are thrown clear while unfired rounds are merely lifted. ⛔ Take the unfired cartridges out by hand.
steps.prose: Which of the two happens tells you which barrel has been used. That is worth knowing before you look down them.
steps.quote: The gun has an extractor with ejector function for each barrel. The ejector function is active for the respective barrel after a round has been fired. When the gun is opened the extractors slightly lift the cartridges that have not been fired and eject the fired cartridges.
steps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 5.6. Unloading the gun — NOTE

steps.title: ⛔ Secure and unload BEFORE taking down
steps.action: Blaser's DANGER block heads the takedown section and its instruction is one line: secure and unload the gun before taking down. On a gun that cocks itself when it opens, that is not a formality.
steps.prose: Opening this gun arms it. Every takedown therefore starts from a confirmed-empty gun, not a closed one.
steps.quote: Secure and unload the gun before
steps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 4. Disassembly — DANGER

steps.title: Forearm catch, then the forearm
steps.action: Press the forearm catch and take the forearm off the radius on the action. ⛔ It has to come off first: Blaser states the barrel set can only be fitted — and by the same token removed — with the forearm already off.
steps.prose: One catch, one part, and the order is not optional.
steps.aside: Inserting the barrel set is only possible with removed forearm.
steps.quote: Remove the forearm as follows: • Press the forearm catch. • Remove the forearm.
steps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 4.1. Removing the forearm

steps.title: Barrel set off at about 45°
steps.action: Press the locking lever and keep it pressed, tip the barrel set to roughly 45°, and pull the hinge pin in the action out of its housings on the barrel set. ⚠ Forty-five degrees, not fully open — the pin only clears part-way through the swing.
steps.prose: Fully open is where you load. Part-open is where it comes apart.
steps.quote: Remove barrel set as follows: • Press locking lever and keep pressed.
steps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 4.2. Removing the barrel set

steps.title: ⚠ Barrel sets and forearms — the gauge rule runs ONE WAY
steps.action: The F3 takes barrel sets in 12, 20 and 28 gauge. Blaser's compatibility note is directional: a SMALLER-gauge barrel can be used with a LARGER-gauge forearm — a 28 with a 20 or 12 forearm — but NOT the other way round. ⛔ And before loading, confirm the ammunition matches the barrel combination actually fitted.
steps.prose: A multi-gauge gun on the bench is a multi-gauge gun in the cabinet. The check belongs to every session.
steps.quote: Barrels with smaller gauges can also be used with forearms of larger gauges. A barrel in 28 gauge can also be used with a forearm in 20 or 12 gauge. Though this is not possible vice versa.
steps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 3.1. Mounting the barrel set — NOTE
steps.warn: The gun can also be supplied with barrel sets in 12, 20 and 28 gauge. Please make sure before loading that the ammunition corresponds with the barrel combination.

steps.title: That is the strip — and Blaser stops here
steps.action: Forearm, barrel set, action-and-stock. Nothing further is published for the owner. ⚠ Even §6.2's damper for the top firing pin is explicitly marked as needing no maintenance at all.
steps.prose: Three parts. Clean it as three parts and put the tools away.
steps.quote: The damper for the top firing pin is fixed with the threaded rod of the balancer and has a spring mounted central firing bolt made from brass. Maintenance on this part is not necessary.
steps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 6.2. Damper for top firing pin

deepSteps.title: ⛔ SuperTrap only — the rail sets the point of impact, one click at a time
deepSteps.action: §6 is this model's own section. To move the point of impact you change the RAIL ANGLE: unscrew the locking screw (SW1.3) fully to activate the click locking and free the rail adjustment screw, then turn the rail adjustment screw. ⚠ One click is HALF A TURN and moves the point of impact 1 cm at 35 m.
deepSteps.prose: A number you can count in clicks beats a number you have to guess at from a pattern board.
deepSteps.aside: In order to change the barrel set’s point of impact, the rail angle has to be adjusted through the rail adjustment.
deepSteps.quote: By turning the rail adjustment screw (SW1.3), the angle of the barrel rail is changed. The integrated click adjustment provides that one click (corresponds half a turn) changes the point of impact by 1 cm at a target distance of 35 m.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 6.1. Adjusting the point of impact

deepSteps.title: Lock the rail back down — and it is thermo stable
deepSteps.action: Once the rail adjustment screw has locked and the point of impact is where you want it, screw the locking screw (SW1.3) fully back in. That locks the adjustment, and Blaser notes the arrangement is THERMO STABLE — it does not wander with temperature.
deepSteps.prose: Finishing the adjustment means putting the lock back, not just stopping turning.
deepSteps.quote: Once the rail adjustment screw has locked and the desired point of impact is adjusted, the locking screw (SW1.3) can be screwed in fully. Thus the rail adjustment screw is locked. The rail adjustment is thermo stable.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 6.1. Adjusting the point of impact

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The USGL threaded rod is under STRIKER SPRING FORCE
deepSteps.action: If your SuperTrap carries the USGL barrel balancers, the threaded rod in the top chamber comes out with a 5 mm Allen key — and Blaser warns that the key must be pressed FIRMLY against the striker pin's spring force to avoid slipping off. ⛔ Forearm and barrel set come off first, on a secured and unloaded gun.
deepSteps.prose: A hex key skating out of a socket that is pushing back is how a rib gets scarred.
deepSteps.quote: the Allen Key must be pressed firmly against the striker pin‘s spring force to avoid slipping off
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 6.3. Mounting the barrel balancers USGL

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Steel shot and the tight chokes — and the book contradicts itself
deepSteps.action: Blaser bars the tight chokes with steel, tungsten, tungsten-iron or molyshot, and bars firing with no choke fitted at all. ⚠ THE BOOK PRINTS THIS DANGER BLOCK TWICE WITH DIFFERENT LISTS — §5.9 bars 3/4 (IM), 1/1 (F) and 5/4 (EF) and above; §5.10 bars only 3/4 (IM) and 1/1 (F). This guide carries the WIDER list, because the safe reading of two disagreeing warnings is the one that forbids more.
deepSteps.prose: When a maker disagrees with himself about a barrel-damage warning, take the stricter half and say why.
deepSteps.aside: The F3 Shotgun is steel shot proofed and is steel shot compatible.
deepSteps.quote: If steel shot, tungsten, tungsten iron or molyshot are used, do not use interchangeable chokes of sizes 3/4 (im), 1/1 (f) or 5/4 (ef) and above.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 5.9. Steel shot cartridges — DANGER
deepSteps.warn: Only fire with fitted interchangeable chokes.

deepSteps.title: Changing chokes — open gun, clean fine threads, the key
deepSteps.action: Engage the safety and unload before a choke is touched, and change them only with the gun OPEN. Blaser's second DANGER block is about the threads: they are FINE threads, they must be clean and lightly oiled, and only the supplied choke key is used.
deepSteps.prose: Fine threads in a barrel muzzle are unforgiving of grit and of improvised tools alike.
deepSteps.aside: Only use the supplied choke key for
deepSteps.quote: Engage safety and unload the gun before
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 5.10. Interchangeable chokes — DANGER

deepSteps.title: Letting the locks down — DUMMY ROUNDS
deepSteps.action: This gun cocks both locks as it opens, so it can go away cocked. Blaser's method is dummy rounds: unload first, barrel tilted down, dummy cartridges into the chambers, buttstock up, locking lever checked with the index finger, then the trigger pulled twice. ⚠ Blaser also flags the obvious hazard — a dummy round and a live round are confusable.
deepSteps.prose: Two pulls, two locks. Doing it on empty chambers is how firing pins end.
deepSteps.aside: Decock the locks as follow: • Hold the barrel tilted downwards.
deepSteps.quote: Decocking the locks using dummy rounds.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 5.8. Decocking the firing blocks

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Barrel selection is an OPEN-LOCK operation, and this gun is handed
deepSteps.action: The barrel selector sits in front of the trigger and picks which barrel fires first. ⛔ Blaser's DANGER block says selection is only performed with the lock OPEN. ⚠ Note also that unlike the F16, the F3 is built for right AND left-handed users, and the locking lever opens to whichever side the version is made for.
deepSteps.prose: If the lever opens the 'wrong' way on yours, it may be the left-handed version rather than a fault.
deepSteps.aside: The F3 Shotgun is designed for right and left-handed users. The locking lever is opened in accordance with the version to the right (for right-handed users) or to the left (for left-handed users).
deepSteps.quote: A barrel selector lever is located in front of the trigger for selecting the barrel for the first and second shot.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F3 — BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 04-2014 — read from the document's own footer — 5.7. Barrel selection and firing
deepSteps.warn: Only perform selection with opened lock.

cleaning.name: BARRELS AND CHOKES
tasks: Bores cleaned; chambers wiped dry after use
Choke fine threads kept clean and LIGHTLY OILED
⛔ Never fired with no interchangeable choke fitted

cleaning.name: ACTION AND LOCKS
tasks: Hinge and locking surfaces wiped and lightly greased
⛔ Trigger NOT touched while the gun is being closed
Locks let down on dummy rounds before storage, never on empty chambers

cleaning.name: RIB AND STOCK
tasks: ⚠ SuperTrap only — rail adjustment and locking screws checked tight
Adjustable comb fixing screws A and B checked after a strip
Recoil-pad fixing screws matched to the number of spacers fitted

reassembly: Locking lever pressed until it engages; both extractors pushed in to the stop.
⛔ Forearm OFF while the barrel set goes on — Blaser states it is the only way.
Hinge pin into its housings with the barrel set angled down, then the buttstock tipped up.
⛔ Locking lever checked closed WITH THE INDEX FINGER, not by eye.
Forearm onto the radius on the action and tipped up until it engages.
Safety catch back — S visible — before the gun leaves the bench.
fncheck: With the gun confirmed unloaded, close it and check the locking lever with your INDEX FINGER — Blaser asks for a physical check in this book too. Work the safety both ways and confirm S and F appear in turn. Move the barrel selector left and right and feel both detents; ⛔ Blaser bars selecting with the lock closed, so do it on an open gun. ⚠ Then let the locks down on DUMMY ROUNDS rather than on empty chambers, and close the gun WITHOUT touching the trigger — on this action a finger on the trigger during closing can block the strikers.
